description: Validates HashiCorp Vault policy definitions for least-privilege compliance, safe capability declarations, and operational accountability

rules.description: vault-policy-spec.json must exist, be valid JSON, and declare name, a non-empty paths array, and a roles array. Every path entry must have a path string and a non-empty capabilities array
Every role referenced in path entries must be declared in the top-level roles array. Undeclared roles produce a runtime auth failure when the service account attempts to authenticate
Paths containing * or + wildcards are flagged unless the entry includes wildcardException with a justification. Wildcards grant access to all current and future secrets under a prefix
rules.note: Exemption: add wildcardException: "reason" to the specific path entry

rules.description: All declared capabilities must be from the recognised Vault capability set. Unrecognised values are silently ignored by Vault, making the policy misleading
Paths under sys/raw, sys/mount, or auth/token/root are restricted. These paths provide cluster-level access and must be explicitly acknowledged with allowRootAccess: true
rules.note: Exemption: set allowRootAccess: true in the spec with a documented justification

rules.description: When spec.allowedPrefixes is declared, every path must start with one of the declared prefixes. Paths outside the allowed set indicate scope creep or misconfiguration
vault-policy-spec.json must not contain TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, or PLACEHOLDER markers

Policy must declare description (for auditor clarity) and owner (for access review accountability). Kubernetes service account roles must specify namespace — missing namespace allows any namespace's SA to authenticate

conditionalRules.hint: Add namespace to scope the Kubernetes auth binding to a specific namespace
